## 4.1 Missing Values & Outliers (Data Quality Check)

### Missing Values
- We checked missingness using `colSums()` / `colMeans()`.
- Most variables show very low missing rate (<5%).
- This suggests the dataset is complete and reliable.

### Outliers
- Boxplots revealed clear extreme values (e.g., leaf size, height).
- These traits require **log transformation** or **capping**.
- Overall: data is usable but needs normalization.

---

## 4.2 Distribution & Class Balance

.pull-left[
### Feature Distribution (Skewness)

<img src="fig_hist.png" style="max-width:60%; height:auto; border:1px solid #ccc; border-radius:6px;">

.smaller[
- Many numeric traits are **right-skewed** (long tail).  
- After log10 transform they become more regular / comparable.  
- Helps ensure large values don't dominate during modelling.
]
]

.pull-right[
### Target Variable (Growth Form)

<img src="fig_target.png" style="max-width:60%; height:auto; border:1px solid #ccc; border-radius:6px;">

.smaller[
- The dataset is **highly imbalanced**.  
- **Shrub** and **Herb** dominate the samples.  
- Rare classes (e.g. climber, fern) are very few.  
- → Apply **class weighting / resampling** later.
]
]

---

## 4.3 Trait Comparison & PCA

.pull-left[
### Trait Differences by Growth Form

<img src="fig_trait_box.png" style="max-width:60%; height:auto; border:1px solid #ccc; border-radius:6px;">

.smaller[
- **Trees / Climbers:** longer leaves, taller growth.  
- **Shrubs / Herbs:** smaller, but wide variation.  
- Confirms growth form impacts plant morphology.
]
]

.pull-right[
### PCA Visualization

<img src="fig_pca.png" style="max-width:60%; height:auto; border:1px solid #ccc; border-radius:6px;">

.smaller[
- PCA (PC1–PC2) shows partial clustering but overlap.  
- PCA emphasizes variance, not class separation.  
- → Supervised models (Decision Tree, XGBoost) can still classify effectively.
]
]
